package: Module, 53 pads (LGA-style castellated-less pads), 13.2 x 16.6 x 2.4 mm
description: Espressif ESP32-C3-MINI-1 & MINI-1U Datasheet v2.2: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi + Bluetooth LE module with on-board PCB antenna (MINI-1), ESP32-C3FH4 chip, 4 MB flash in package. Module size 13.2 x 16.6 x 2.4 mm. VDD33 3.0-3.6V. 53 pads incl. 22 ground pads (1,2,11,14,36-53).

pinout.name: 3V3
pinout.notes: Power supply, VDD33 3.0-3.6V, typ 3.3V (Table 6-2); supply must deliver >=0.5A.

pinout.name: IO2
pinout.notes: GPIO2, ADC1_CH2, FSPIQ. STRAP: Table 4-1 default floating; GPIO2 does not determine SPI boot/Joint Download but should be pulled up (high) due to glitches (Table 4-3 note 2).

pinout.name: EN
pinout.notes: High: on, enables chip. Low: off, chip powers off. Do not leave EN floating (Table 3-1). Chip reset release VIH_nRST = 0.75*VDD1 min. Strapping setup tSU=0ms min before EN high; hold tH=3ms min (Table 4-2).

pinout.name: IO8
pinout.notes: GPIO8. STRAP: Table 4-1 default floating; boot mode: SPI boot = any value, Joint Download boot = 1 (Table 4-3); also ROM message printing strap.

pinout.name: IO9
pinout.notes: GPIO9. STRAP: Table 4-1 default weak pull-up = 1. SPI boot mode requires 1; Joint Download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG or UART download) requires 0 (Table 4-3).

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Central thermal/exposed pad (EPAD), drawn as 3x3 array of GND pads in Fig 3-1/11-1. Soldering to base-board ground is optional but improves thermal performance (Sec 9, p34).

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Corner GND pad (0.7x0.7 mm per Fig 11-1).

decoupling.value: C1 10uF + C2 0.1uF on VDD33 (3V3 rail at module pin 3)
decoupling.placement: at the 3V3 supply entry to the module, to GND (Fig 9-1 Peripheral Schematics, p34)
decoupling.notes: Datasheet reference schematic shows 10uF and 0.1uF in parallel on VDD33; no further placement text in the datasheet.

decoupling.value: EN: R=10 kOhm pull-up to VDD33 (R9) + C=1 uF to GND (C3, shown TBD in Fig 9-1; 1uF per text); 0 ohm series R2 to reset button SW1 with 0.1uF C4 to GND on button side
decoupling.placement: RC delay at EN pin to keep chip supply stable during power-up
decoupling.notes: Sec 9 p34: 'recommended setting for the RC delay circuit is usually R = 10 kOhm and C = 1 uF. However, specific parameters should be adjusted based on the power-up timing of the module and the power-up and reset sequence timing of the chip.' Do not leave EN floating.

land_pattern.notes: From Fig 11-1 (p38, read visually; unit mm): 48 edge pads 0.4 wide x 0.8 long; 4 corner pads (50-53) 0.7 x 0.7; central EPAD (pin 49, GND) is a 3x3 array of 1.45 x 1.45 square pads with 0.6 gaps (5.4 x 5.4 total, thermal vias shown; pin-1 corner chamfered). Pad-row extents: 11.9 / 11.8 across the bottom/top rows, 9.9 / 9.8 and 11.2 along side columns, 1.6 dimension at pad rows, 0.8 pad length. Overall land+antenna area 13.2 wide x 16.6 tall, of which antenna area is 13.2 x 5.4 (16.6 - 11.2) at the top, plus 0.8 below the pad rows. Pin numbering (Fig 3-1 top view, p10): pins 1-11 left column top to bottom, 12-24 bottom row left to right, 25-35 right column bottom to top, 36-48 top row right to left, 49 center, 50 top-right, 51 bottom-right, 52 bottom-left, 53 top-left corner. Pad pitch is not dimensioned in the figure text; take from the STEP/source file (see OPEN).

layout_notes: ANTENNA KEEP-OUT (Fig 3-1 p10, Note A; Fig 11-1 p38): the module's on-board PCB antenna is at one end (top in Fig 3-1) of the 13.2 x 16.6 mm module. The dotted-line antenna keepout zone covers the antenna end of the module outline: full module width 13.2 mm x about 5.4 mm (16.6 - 11.2 mm, Fig 11-1 'Antenna Area'), drawn slightly beyond the module outline. Base-board rule: no copper on any layer, no parts, in this zone. Keep it free of copper (traces, pours, ground, vias) and components on ALL layers.

Placement: datasheet p39 Sec 11.2 says the base board's interference with the antenna must be minimised, and defers exact placement and any base-board keep-out beyond the module-outline zone to ESP32-C3 Hardware Design Guidelines > 'General Principles of PCB Layout for Modules' (NOT in this PDF). Figs 3-1/11-1 show the antenna at the end of the module beyond the top GND pad row (pads 36-48), i.e. the end away from pins 12-24; no numeric board-edge overhang distance is stated.
ESP32-C3-MINI-1U (external antenna connector) has no antenna keepout; this part (MINI-1) does.

EPAD (pin 49): soldering to base-board ground is not a must but optimises thermal performance; apply the correct amount of solder paste - too much paste raises the module-to-board gap and weakens adhesion of the other pads (Sec 9 p34). Figure 11-1 shows thermal vias in the EPAD land.
EN: add RC delay (R=10k, C=1uF) for stable power-up; do not float EN (p34, Table 3-1).

Strapping pins GPIO2, GPIO8, GPIO9 (Table 4-1/4-3): GPIO2 floating default, pull high recommended (glitches); GPIO8 floating default, SPI boot any value, Joint Download needs 1; GPIO9 weak pull-up default=1: 1 = SPI boot (normal), 0 = Joint Download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG / UART download). Strapping is sampled at EN rising; setup tSU >=0 ms, hold tH >=3 ms. Fig 9-1 uses R8 10k pull-up on IO9 with JP2 boot-option jumper to GND.
USB: IO18 = USB_D- (pin 26), IO19 = USB_D+ (pin 27); Fig 9-1 routes them through 0 ohm R6 (D-) and R4 (D+) to USB connector JP3, with TBD caps C5/C6 to GND.
UART0 (RXD0 pin 30 = GPIO20 U0RXD, TXD0 pin 31 = GPIO21 U0TXD) is used to download firmware and log output (p34).
IO0/IO1 can carry a 32.768 kHz crystal (XTAL_32K_P/N); Fig 9-1 shows it as no-component option with 12pF caps.
Recommended operating: VDD33 3.0-3.6V, supply capable of 0.5 A (Table 6-2).
